title: The lullaby
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, quiet suburban house at night, soft green electronic glow and cold moonlight, muted grey-blue palette with warm lamp accents, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 3. She knew every note of the song. Her grandmother sang it. 🎶

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Eli traced the humming to an empty lot where a house burned in 1979. Then the signal moved. Into their house.
scenes.image: a quiet suburban house at night, a faint green glow in the upstairs window

scenes.narration: Dana didn't sleep. She sat up with the monitor in her lap, and when the humming came at 2:10, she did something Eli didn't expect. She hummed along.
scenes.image: a woman sitting cross-legged on a bed in the dark, a glowing monitor in her lap, eyes closed

scenes.narration: She knew every note. She didn't know how. Then the words came back, all at once, from somewhere deep and old.
scenes.image: close-up of a woman's face in green light, tears on her cheek, lips slightly parted

scenes.narration: Hush now, the cold can't find you. Hush now, the door is shut. Her grandmother used to sing it. Every night.
scenes.image: an old knitted cardigan draped over the arm of a chair beside a warm lamp, a faint wisp of woodsmoke

scenes.narration: Grandma Marion. Dana barely remembered her. Just the song, and soft wool, and the smell of woodsmoke.
scenes.image: faded 1970s photograph of a kind older woman in a cardigan sitting on a porch swing

scenes.narration: In the morning, Dana called her mother and asked where Marion lived, before the nursing home.
scenes.image: a woman standing at a kitchen window in grey morning light, holding a phone to her ear

scenes.narration: Her mother went quiet. Then she said a street name. Their street. The house at the end. The one that burned.
scenes.image: the empty overgrown lot at the end of a suburban street in morning fog, concrete steps leading nowhere

scenes.narration: Marion survived the fire. She never talked about it. Only once she said: something wanted in, and I wouldn't let it.
scenes.image: an older woman's hands folded on a quilt by a window, firelight glow reflected in the glass

scenes.narration: That night the humming came again. Dana leaned toward the monitor and whispered: Grandma?
scenes.image: a woman leaning close to a glowing monitor on a nightstand, whispering into it, dark bedroom

scenes.narration: The humming stopped. The rocking stopped. And an old, gentle voice said: there you are. I've been watching your house.
scenes.image: a scorched rocking chair standing still in tall weeds under moonlight, facing a row of distant houses
